title: mcp-trace-validator JSON report
description: The output of `mcp-trace-validator validate --format json`: a single-revision report, a multi-revision one when several revisions were judged, or, for several traces, an envelope holding one of those per trace. It describes the release it ships with, closed (`additionalProperties: false`) so a test can prove every emitted member is documented; a later release may add members, and says so in its changelog. Absent optional members mean 'nothing to say' — they are omitted rather than written as null or empty.

traceReports.description: Several traces judged in one run (`validate` given more than one trace): each trace's report in the shape it would have alone, the most severe verdict across them, and the named traces that could not be judged at all, with why (also on stderr; they count toward the exit status).

verdict.description: The most severe of the traces' verdicts, or `incomplete` when any named trace could not be judged — whatever the judged ones say, the run did not judge them all, and it exits 2 or 3.

trace.description: The trace as it was named on the command line.

unjudged.description: How many named traces could not be judged: unreadable, malformed, of an unsupported revision, or judging nothing.

unjudged_traces.description: Each trace counted in `unjudged`, in the order named, with the error that kept it from being judged. Present exactly when `unjudged` is not 0.

trace.description: The trace as it was named on the command line.

error.description: Why it could not be judged: the error line `validate` printed on stderr, without its `error: ` prefix.

revisionSource.description: How the judged revision(s) were chosen: named on the command line, declared by the trace, or the newest supported because the trace declared none.

revisionMismatch.description: The revisions the session declared, present only when none of them was judged: the outcomes judge the trace against rules it was not playing by.

actor.description: The party a clause binds, as the registry states it (`mcp-trace-validator requirements --format json` prints the same member).

partyView.description: The party the report is viewed for (`validate --party`): only findings whose `party` is this one, or absent, count toward `verdict` and the exit status. The rows and totals are unchanged by the view. Absent by default, when every finding counts.

totals.description: Requirements per outcome; they sum to the number of requirements judged.

verdict.description: Follows from the totals: unsupported if any clause is, else fail if any fails, else pass-with-warnings if any warns, else pass. Under a `party_view` the same ranking is applied to the findings that count — a failing or warning row, and a failed wire schema, counts only through a finding whose `party` is the viewed one or absent. The exit code maps it: fail is 1 (as is pass-with-warnings under --strict), unsupported is 2.

finding.description: One violation: the check that found it, the event it points at when one is identifiable, the party it is held against when the trace can say, and what was wrong.

party.description: The party the finding is held against: the clause's actor when it binds one party; for a clause binding both, the sender of the message at `seq`. Absent when neither decides it — no `seq`, or an event there that is not a message — rather than guessed.

source.description: The clause a failing or warning row breaks: its spec page and anchor, the clause verbatim, and its published link — at the judged revision, or, for an extension's clause, where the extension's own repository publishes it (ADR-0023).

row.description: One requirement's outcome. `findings` and `source` accompany `fail` and `warn`; `exclusion` accompanies `excluded`; `missing_checks` accompanies `unsupported`; `capability` accompanies `not-applicable`.

wireSchema.description: Every message held to the judged revision's own JSON Schema, vendored from the specification (the `schema` URL pins the upstream commit). Not a requirement row and not counted in `totals`, but a `fail` fails the verdict. Absent when the build vendors no schema for the revision.

traceEnding.description: What the recorder saw last: an orderly `transport-close`, a `transport-abort`, or a message or HTTP event (the recording simply stopped).

unansweredRequest.description: One request the trace ended without answering.

id.description: The request's `id`, as sent — whatever JSON value it was.

sender.description: Who sent the request, and so who was owed the answer.

unansweredRequests.description: The requests that had no response when the trace ended: a note. JSON-RPC expects every request answered, but no judgeable clause of either revision states it, so this moves neither the totals nor the verdict. A request its sender cancelled (`notifications/cancelled` naming its id) is not counted, nor is one answered later out of order; one the HTTP layer refused before reading it (401, 403) was never a message the protocol saw. Absent when every request was answered.

requests.description: The first ten, in `seq` order; `count` says how many there were.

report.description: One trace judged against one revision.

extensions.description: The extensions the session exercised, each judged against its own clauses and never scored: nothing here moves the report's `totals` or `verdict`, the way the official suite runs an extension's scenarios under `not_scored: extension` (ADR-0023). An extension appears once one of its clauses passed, failed, warned or is unsupported; omitted when none did.

extension.description: One extension's clauses: its own verdict and totals, derived as a report's are and read by nothing else.

verdict.description: What the extension's clauses add up to, for its implementers; informational, never an exit status.

multiRow.description: One clause across the judged revisions; each array is aligned by index with `revisions`. A null outcome means the clause does not exist at that revision. `findings` and `sources` are omitted when no revision has any.

multiReport.description: One trace judged against several revisions, aligned per clause.

verdict.description: The worst of the per-revision verdicts (each of which honours `party_view`).

unanswered_requests.description: The trace's unanswered requests, the same under every revision, so carried once.
